JIRAASF JIRA5aa69414-a9e9-3523-82ec-879b028fb15bKAFKA-20734
Motivation
Share groups distribute records from the same topic partition across multiple consumers. Applications may subsequently need to process a selected subset of those records again without repeating unrelated completed work.
Examples include correcting a transformation, reprocessing inputs affected by an application defect, or restoring the exact inputs recorded in a durable processing manifest.
Existing mechanisms do not directly support this requirement:
RELEASE relinquishes currently acquired records; it does not reopen previously completed records.
ShareConsumer does not provide ordinary consumerassignandseeksemantics.
Share-group offset reset requires an empty group and initializes partition state rather than preserving an arbitrary sparse selection of completed records.Existing API contract (https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/bb6c417e57a001fee77c6909fa03230bc7d496b1/clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/clients/admin/Admin.java#L2018).
Consider records previously processed by two workers:
| Offsets, inclusive | Previous processing | Required behavior
| 100–104 | Worker A | Make available again
| 105–149 | Worker B | Preserve completion
| 150–154 | Worker A | Make available again
| 155–199 | Other completed work | Preserve completion
The application needs to select100–104and150–154without making B’s records available again.
This proposal introducesselective redelivery:
Make an explicitly selected set of retained records AVAILABLE for delivery again in the same share group, while preserving delivery eligibility and retained processing metadata outside that selection.
Successful completion confirms a durable eligibility change. It does not confirm that the records have already been delivered or processed.
Public Interfaces
ShareConsumer API
Introduce an asynchronous operation onShareConsumer:ShareRedeliveryResult requestRedelivery(ShareRedeliveryRequest request);
The API names are proposed and subject to review.
The consumer’s configured group ID scopes the operation. No Admin client is required.
Each partition selection contains:
Topic UUID and partition.
Sorted, non-overlapping, half-open offset ranges.
A caller-generated operation ID that survives application restart.
An expected state token identifying the group-state lineage and availability revision.
For example,[100, 105)and[150, 155)select the records in the motivation.
Companion interfaces provide the current state token and inspect an operation after a client restart or lost response.
Result contract
ShareRedeliveryResultexposes per-partition futures and an aggregate future.
| Outcome | Contract
| APPLIED | The eligibility change and operation result are durable, and stale processing is fenced.
| ALREADY_AVAILABLE | The selection required no new delivery cycle at the operation’s linearization point.
| REJECTED / BUSY | The operation definitively made no change for that partition.
| Timeout or lost response | The outcome is unknown; inspect or retry the same operation ID.
Atomicity is per share partition. Requests spanning multiple partitions may partially succeed.
Any eligible member may acquire the selected records. The requester receives no exclusive ownership.
Network protocol and persistence
Introduce protocol support for requesting redelivery, obtaining state tokens, and inspecting operation results.
Extend acquisition and acknowledgement metadata with generation information sufficient to reject delayed operations from an earlier delivery cycle.
Introduce versioned share-coordinator records for operation identity, lifecycle, availability revision, preserved exclusion cover
